title: Northern Han
capsule: Northern Han (北漢, Běi Hàn) was a small Chinese dynastic state centered on Taiyuan in Shanxi, founded in 951 by Liu Min after the fall of the Later Han dynasty and lasting as the final survivor of the Ten Kingdoms. Squeezed between the successive Five Dynasties regimes to the south and the Liao dynasty (Khitan) to the north, Northern Han relied on Liao military backing to survive repeated Song offensives. Emperor Taizong of Song personally besieged Taiyuan in 979, and the last ruler Liu Jiyuan surrendered in the fifth month of that year, ending the state after twenty-eight years. Song forces then demolished Taiyuan city and relocated its population, erasing Northern Han's capital as a deliberate act of pacification.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core territory of Northern Han around the Fen River valley in Shanxi is reliably attested; outer boundaries fluctuated with Liao support and Song military pressure and are only approximately known.
